scenes.title: Choose the first digit
scenes.narration: Use two different digits chosen from one, two and three. List all the possible two-digit numbers in increasing order. Think about which position decides the order first.

scenes.title: Finish every digit drawer
scenes.narration: Start with tens digit one. The other two digits are the only possible ones digits, so write those endings in order. Repeat with each remaining tens digit. The complete list is twelve, thirteen, twenty-one, twenty-three, thirty-one and thirty-two.

scenes.title: Read two labelled counters
scenes.narration: Two numbered counters A and B show whole numbers from one to eight. Their values sum to thirteen. How many possible ordered pairs of readings are there? A and B are distinct counters.

scenes.title: List each ordered pair
scenes.narration: B equals thirteen minus A. Since B is at most eight, A must be at least five. The cap on A is eight. Every integer in that inclusive range gives one legal B, for four pairs.

scenes.title: Open three labelled boxes
scenes.narration: Three labelled boxes A, B and C contain a total of eleven tokens. Each holds between one and six tokens inclusive. A holds an even number. Count the different ordered triples of box sizes. The boxes keep their labels.

scenes.title: Set the limits of each row
scenes.narration: The possible values for A are two, four and six. Make a row for each one. In each row B plus C is eleven minus A. Requiring C to be at most six gives a lower bound on B. Requiring C to be positive gives the upper bound. Use the cap of six on B as well, then count the range inclusively.

scenes.title: Count the fourteen triples
scenes.narration: The row counts are four, six and four, so there are fourteen triples altogether. Each legal triple has exactly one value for A. Within that row a legal B fixes C, so every triple is covered exactly once.

scenes.title: Pack two unlabelled parcels
scenes.narration: Two parcels weigh ten kilograms together. Each weighs a whole number from one to eight kilograms. Swapping the parcels makes the same load. How many loads are possible? Write the lighter weight first. It starts at two, because the other parcel cannot exceed eight. It ends at five, because the lighter weight cannot exceed half the total. The pairs are two and eight, three and seven, four and six, and five and five. Four loads, with the equal pair counted once.
